questions.question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). F is sitting third to the left of A. A is sitting second to the left of G. G is sitting to the immediate right of E. B is sitting to the immediate left of D. What is the position of F with respect to E?
questions.solution:
**Given:** A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1) F is sitting third to the left of A.

2) A is sitting second to the left of G.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59e35bd474108edcb1f342e353380cbf7650f1d875369c156915c0e456cb102f.png] 

3) G is sitting to the immediate right of E.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0eb4f6b1493834635f5ca19a55e27f7778cfc94e5a19c24071dcedec52eabc2a.png] 

4) B is sitting to the immediate left of D.

After positioning B and D only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a7f575abb4948913f5f3e7b5443160a681d89d1468145d2c9bf02d5dc5b1bcf2.png] 

Thus, according to the final arrangement, F is third to the right E.

Hence, **"Option 3"** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All doors are locks.

Some locks are handles,

Conclusions:

(I) All handles are locks.

(II) No door is a handle.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/014960155d56f86c9f63002525db78172cdcf7b1fc24460be30719d6210b884b.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) All handles are locks → Does not follow (As some locks are handles. So it is possible but not definite.)

(II) No door is a handle → Does not follow (As all doors are locks and some locks are handles. As no direct relation is given between doors and handles, therefore it is false.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2"

questions.question:
T, N, S, P, R and M are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). S is sitting second to the left of T. Only two people are sitting between S and R. M is not the immediate neighbour of S. P is sitting second to the right of R.

How many people are sitting between N and M, when counted from the right of N?
questions.solution:
Given: T, N, S, P, R and M are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1) S is sitting second to the left of T. 

2) Only two people are sitting between S and R.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/292c2479e5ba63fce7fe738fcaa70b14f137471275597173b2a0cf10f3241408.png] 

3) M is not the immediate neighbour of S.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3736359cbc5004f52310fe8f458b78f5d72661305a4aa03ee517165dd305e0ae.png] 

4) P is sitting second to the right of R.

After positioning P only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. N.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb552d8fb5b91536b6ed3788a5b66122c36be864ad8e46a7df800f3c50c8cd33.png] 

Thus, according to the final arrangement, two people are sitting between N and M, when counted from the right of N.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

11, 66

26, 156
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

11, 66 → 11 × 6 = 66

And,

26, 156 → 26 × 6 = 156

So, checking each option one by one:

Option 1) 26, 152 → 26 × 6 = 156 ≠ 152

Option 2) **18, 108 → 18 × 6 = 108**

Option 3) 20, 130 → 20 × 6 = 120 ≠ 130

Option 4) 15, 75 → 15 × 6 = 90 ≠ 75

Thus, out of all the options '18, 108' follows the same logic as given.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s).

Statements:

All cabbages are roses.

All cabbages are tulips.

Conclusions:

(I) At least some tulips are roses.

(II) All roses are cabbages.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ca9b3251b43954d058b53429c49e8a4a631ba7d918a9e7279fb07750ed3ee31.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) At least some tulips are roses → Follow (As all cabbages are roses and all cabbages are tulips. As whole cabbages comes in both roses and tulips, therefore some roses are tulips.)

(II) All roses are cabbages → Does not follow (As all cabbages are roses. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion (I) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4"
